question: A 74-year-old man is brought to the physician by his wife for progressively worsening confusion and forgetfulness. Vital signs are within normal limits. Physical examination shows a flat affect and impaired short-term memory. An MRI of the brain is shown. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Progressively worsening confusion and forgetfulness" -> "Impaired short-term memory" -> "Flat affect" -> "MRI of the brain findings" -> "Cortical atrophy" -> 80% CHAIN: "Progressively worsening confusion and forgetfulness" -> "Impaired short-term memory" -> "Flat affect" -> "MRI of the brain findings" -> "Enlarged ventricles" -> 75% CHAIN: "Progressively worsening confusion and forgetfulness" -> "Impaired short-term memory" -> "Flat affect" -> "MRI of the brain findings" -> "White matter changes" -> 80%
analysis: The patient is presenting with symptoms of progressive cognitive decline, flat affect, and impaired short-term memory, which are indicative of a neurodegenerative disorder such as Alzheimer's disease. The MRI findings are likely to show atrophy of the brain, particularly in the temporal and parietal lobes. This atrophy is characteristic of Alzheimer's disease.
